# Language Lineage — Full Site Reference

Language Lineage is a structured knowledge base for programming-language implementation and influence relationships. It answers questions such as what Python is written in, how Rust is bootstrapped, and which languages influenced JavaScript.

## Dataset

- Version: 5.0
- Total nodes: 152
- Language nodes: 131
- Tool nodes: 21
- Relationships: 443
- Evidence coverage: every relationship has at least one source URL
- License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
- Download: https://www.languagelineage.org/dataset/v5/lineage_v5.json
- Artifact page: https://www.languagelineage.org/dataset

## Relationship types

| Type | Count |
|---|---:|
| influenced | 252 |
| compiler_written_in | 96 |
| runtime_written_in | 67 |
| bootstrap_written_in | 15 |
| transpiled_to | 11 |
| rewritten_in | 2 |

## Data schema

Language and tool nodes include identity, release year, implementation, paradigm, typing, runtime, self-hosting, cluster, enrichment, and logo metadata. Relationships include source and target identifiers, relationship type, date range, confidence, evidence URL, and notes.

## Citation

Language Lineage. Programming Language Lineage Dataset, v5.0. 152 nodes and 443 relationships. https://www.languagelineage.org/dataset

- [V8 vs SpiderMonkey vs JavaScriptCore | Language Lineage](https://www.languagelineage.org/guides/v8-vs-spidermonkey-vs-javascriptcore): All three major JavaScript engines are written in C++. V8 powers Chrome and Node.js, SpiderMonkey powers Firefox, and JavaScriptCore powers Safari.
- [TypeScript vs JavaScript Compilers: tsc, swc, esbuild | Language Lineage](https://www.languagelineage.org/guides/typescript-vs-javascript-implementation): TypeScript adds types to JavaScript. The official compiler tsc is self-hosting TypeScript; swc is written in Rust; esbuild is written in Go. All three transpile to JavaScript.
- [GraalVM vs HotSpot: Two JVM Implementations Compared | Language Lineage](https://www.languagelineage.org/guides/graalvm-vs-hotspot): HotSpot (C and C++) is the standard JVM in OpenJDK. GraalVM replaces the C2 JIT with a Java-written compiler and adds polyglot and Native Image support. Both run the same bytecode.
- [How Modern Languages Trace Their Toolchains Back to C | Language Lineage](https://www.languagelineage.org/guides/the-c-bootstrap-chain): How Python, Rust, Go, JavaScript, Java, Ruby, and Haskell trace their compiler or runtime implementation back to C or C++. 7 chains computed from the Language Lineage dataset.
